newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to attend services for his great uncle.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to attend services for his great uncle.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will attend funeral services for his great uncle in Arkansas on Thursday, forcing him to reschedule a speech before the United Nations to later in the day, the White House said on Tuesday.
Henry Oren Grisham, called "Uncle Buddy" by Clinton, died on Monday night at a nursing home in Hope, Arkansas, the president's birthplace. He was 92 and had been in poor health for some time.

Clinton, who flies to Tennessee on Wednesday to participate in a conference on families hosted by Vice President Al Gore and then goes to Chicago for a fundraiser for Sen. Carol Moseley-Braun, will fly to Arkansas that night.
Clinton, who had been scheduled to deliver a morning address at the United Nations on environmental issues on Thursday, planned to speak to the world body later in the day.
Grisham, an uncle of Clinton's mother, will be buried on Thursday in Hope.

"He was a lifelong influence on the president," Janie Brazzel, a friend of the Grisham family, said. "He was a very sincere, very likeable gentleman and I know the president is going to miss him terribly."
Clinton's father, William Blythe, died shortly before he was born and Grisham was a steady presence in Clinton's upbringing.
Born on Dec. 11, 1904, near Hope, Grisham worked as a firefighter at a military ordnance plant in Texas and later owned a pastry shop in Hope.
He is survived by four children.
